suggestions.rationale: Post-traumatic headache is a recognized complication after mild traumatic brain injury, and its clinical phenotype can overlap with migraine or tension-type headache. Because the catalog target here is `migraine-headaches` rather than the distinct diagnosis of post-traumatic headache, this entry is retained only as a phenotype-oriented research flag for cases in which a clinician has diagnosed persistent post-traumatic headache with migraine features or has separately diagnosed migraine after the documented mTBI. PMID 38568491 supports post-traumatic headache after mTBI and migraine-like phenotype overlap; it does not by itself establish that mTBI caused a primary or secondary migraine diagnosis. Verification therefore remains on hold at the current target taxonomy. Individual review must establish headache onset chronology, diagnostic phenotype, pre-injury headache history, and competing headache causes.
evidenceGaps: Neurology or headache-specialist diagnosis distinguishing migraine from other post-traumatic headache phenotypes
Headache onset chronology relative to the mild TBI, including the temporal criteria used for post-traumatic headache
Headache frequency, duration, associated migraine features, and longitudinal treatment records
Pre-injury headache or migraine history and other competing headache causes
Clinician assessment addressing whether the individual's diagnosed migraine/post-traumatic headache phenotype is attributable to the documented mTBI

sourceReferences.citation: Schwedt TJ. Posttraumatic Headache. Continuum (Minneap Minn). 2024;30(2):411-424. PMID 38568491
sourceReferences.note: Clinical review describes post-traumatic headache attributed to mild TBI, including ICHD-3 temporal criteria and overlap with migraine and tension-type headache phenotypes. Because the repository target is `migraine-headaches` rather than post-traumatic headache, Batch 8 keeps this source unverified for target-level citation verification and uses it only as phenotype-oriented research evidence.
